Fluffy, light, oh-so-soft and topped with a creamy coconut frosting. If you are a coconut lover, this cake is for you!</em></p>
<p><img fetchpriority="high" decoding="async" class="alignnone size-full wp-image-9149" src="https://www.noracooks.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/04/IMG_1772.jpg" alt="looking down on a piece of coconut cake, bite taken" width="667" height="1000" data-pin-description="This is the easiest vegan coconut cake ever, made in 1 bowl with simple ingredients. Fluffy, light, so soft and topped with a creamy coconut frosting. If you are a coconut lover, this cake is for you! #vegan #plantbased" srcset="https://www.noracooks.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/04/IMG_1772.jpg 667w, https://www.noracooks.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/04/IMG_1772-200x300.jpg 200w" sizes="(max-width: 667px) 100vw, 667px" /></p>
<p>I am beyond thrilled with how this cake turned out! It took a few attempts to get it just right, and I’m so excited to share it with you.</p>
<p>I worked hard to make the recipe as <strong>EASY</strong> as possible, with the end result still tasting like something you’d get from a bakery. I love 1 bowl recipes when it comes to baking, and I was able to achieve it here!</p>
<p><strong>Vegan coconut cake is ultra fluffy and soft.</strong> It’s light and moist, instead of being heavy and dense. I used a simple vegan cream cheese coconut flavored frosting, with thin layers of frosting on the cake. <strong>This cake is truly delightful, and I can’t wait for you to try it!</strong><span id="more-9145"></span></p>
<p><img decoding="async" class="alignnone size-full wp-image-9152 perfmatters-lazy" src="data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20width='667'%20height='1000'%20viewBox='0%200%20667%201000'%3E%3C/svg%3E" alt="piece of coconut cake standing up, shot from side, grey background" width="667" height="1000" data-pin-description="This is the easiest vegan coconut cake ever, made in 1 bowl with simple ingredients. Fluffy, light, so soft and topped with a creamy coconut frosting. If you are a coconut lover, this cake is for you! #vegan #plantbased" data-src="https://www.noracooks.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/04/IMG_1749.jpg" data-srcset="https://www.noracooks.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/04/IMG_1749.jpg 667w, https://www.noracooks.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/04/IMG_1749-200x300.jpg 200w" data-sizes="(max-width: 667px) 100vw, 667px" /></p>
<h2>How to make it</h2>
<p>It really could not be easier!</p>
<ol>
<li>Whisk the dry ingredients in a bowl – flour, cornstarch, baking powder, salt and sugar.</li>
<li>Add wet ingredients and mix until just combined – oil, non-dairy milk, vinegar, vanilla and coconut extracts.</li>
<li>Pour into greased pans and bake.</li>
<li>Let cool, then frost.</li>
</ol>

Fluffy, light, so soft and topped with a creamy coconut frosting. If you are a coconut lover, this cake is for you! #vegan #plantbased" data-src="https://www.noracooks.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/04/collage-3.jpg" data-srcset="https://www.noracooks.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/04/collage-3.jpg 800w, https://www.noracooks.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/04/collage-3-240x300.jpg 240w, https://www.noracooks.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/04/collage-3-768x960.jpg 768w" data-sizes="(max-width: 800px) 100vw, 800px" /></p>
<h2>Tips for the best cake</h2>
<ul>
<li><strong>Grease your pans well and line with a circle of parchment paper.</strong> This will prevent your cake from sticking and breaking.</li>
<li><strong>Do not over mix the cake batter!</strong> Your cake will lose it’s fluffiness if you do.</li>
<li><strong>Cool the cakes completely before frosting</strong>, or the cake will slip and break. Also, since this calls for vegan cream cheese frosting, you will need to keep the cake refrigerated so it doesn’t get melty.</li>
<li><strong>Don’t have access to vegan cream cheese?</strong> No problem! Follow the recipe for <a href="https://www.noracooks.com/vanilla-vegan-frosting/">Vegan Vanilla Frosting</a> instead, adding a teaspoon of coconut extract.</li>
</ul>

<div id="recipe-9159-instructions" class="wprm-recipe-instructions-container wprm-recipe-9159-instructions-container wprm-block-text-normal" data-recipe="9159"><h3 class="wprm-recipe-header wprm-recipe-instructions-header wprm-block-text-none wprm-align-left wprm-header-decoration-none wprm-header-has-actions" style="">Instructions </h3><div class="wprm-recipe-instruction-group"><h4 class="wprm-recipe-group-name wprm-recipe-instruction-group-name wprm-block-text-bold">Make the cake</h4><ul class="wprm-recipe-instructions"><li id="wprm-recipe-9159-step-0-0" class="wprm-recipe-instruction" style="list-style-type: decimal;"><div class="wprm-recipe-instruction-text"><span style="display: block;">Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F and grease two 8 inch cake pans. I also like to place a circle of parchment paper on the bottom of each pan for easy removal.</span></div></li><li id="wprm-recipe-9159-step-0-1" class="wprm-recipe-instruction" style="list-style-type: decimal;"><div class="wprm-recipe-instruction-text"><span style="display: block;">In a large bowl, add the flour, cornstarch, baking powder, salt and sugar. Whisk well to combine. </span></div></li><li id="wprm-recipe-9159-step-0-2" class="wprm-recipe-instruction" style="list-style-type: decimal;"><div class="wprm-recipe-instruction-text"><span style="display: block;">To the bowl with the dry ingredients, pour in the oil, non-dairy milk, apple cider vinegar, vanilla and coconut extract. Mix with a large spoon until just combined, but be careful not to over mix the batter or your cake won't be soft and fluffy.</span></div></li><li id="wprm-recipe-9159-step-0-3" class="wprm-recipe-instruction" style="list-style-type: decimal;"><div class="wprm-recipe-instruction-text"><span style="display: block;">Pour into prepared pans and bake for 30-35 minutes, until a toothpick inserted in the middle comes out clean.</span></div></li><li id="wprm-recipe-9159-step-0-4" class="wprm-recipe-instruction" style="list-style-type: decimal;"><div class="wprm-recipe-instruction-text"><span style="display: block;">Let the cakes cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then carefully remove them and place on a cooling rack. Allow the cakes to cool completely before frosting; you can move them to the refrigerator to speed this up. </span></div></li></ul></div><div class="wprm-recipe-instruction-group"><h4 class="wprm-recipe-group-name wprm-recipe-instruction-group-name wprm-block-text-bold">Make the frosting</h4><ul class="wprm-recipe-instructions"><li id="wprm-recipe-9159-step-1-0" class="wprm-recipe-instruction" style="list-style-type: decimal;"><div class="wprm-recipe-instruction-text"><span style="display: block;">To a large bowl (you can simply wipe out the bowl you used for the cake), add vegan cream cheese, slightly softened vegan butter (not too soft, or your frosting will be melty), 3 cups of powdered sugar, vanilla and coconut extract.</span></div></li><li id="wprm-recipe-9159-step-1-1" class="wprm-recipe-instruction" style="list-style-type: decimal;"><div class="wprm-recipe-instruction-text"><span style="display: block;">With a hand mixer, or stand mixer, mix starting on low, then increase to high until all ingredients are combined and smooth. If the frosting seems too runny, add another cup of powdered sugar. If it still is a bit runny, you can stick it in the refrigerator for 30 minutes or so until it firms up a bit.</span></div></li><li id="wprm-recipe-9159-step-1-2" class="wprm-recipe-instruction" style="list-style-type: decimal;"><div class="wprm-recipe-instruction-text"><span style="display: block;">Frost the cake as desired, then sprinkle with shredded coconut and serve. Enjoy!</span></div></li></ul></div></div>

<div id="recipe-9159-notes" class="wprm-recipe-notes-container wprm-block-text-normal"><h3 class="wprm-recipe-header wprm-recipe-notes-header wprm-block-text-none wprm-align-left wprm-header-decoration-none" style="">Notes</h3><div class="wprm-recipe-notes"><ol>
<li>You could substitute cake flour for all purpose if desired, but if you do omit the cornstarch as well. Gluten free all purpose flour may work, but I haven't tested it.</li>
<li>I used melted coconut oil, but you can use canola oil or melted vegan butter as well.</li>
<li>I loved the cake with a cream cheese frosting, but you could also use my <a href="https://www.noracooks.com/vanilla-vegan-frosting/">Vegan Vanilla Frosting</a> and add 1 teaspoon of coconut extract to it.</li>
</ol></div></div>

									</footer><!-- .comment-meta -->

				<div class="comment-content">
					<p>Thanks Susan! A few things that will help the cake not be dry. First, be careful not to over bake it. Only bake until it’s done. Maybe you baked it for too long, causing it to dry out. Second, don’t serve the cake straight from the fridge. A cold cake is going to be a dry, crumbly cake. Let it sit at room temperature for quite a while (30 minutes to an hour) before serving for a moist cake. Cake is almost always going to taste dry and be crumbly when cold. I don’t think you need to add anything else to the cake, I make it often and it’s perfectly moist and fluffy as written. I think your biggest issue is probably the fact your serving it cold.
